content: I want to formalize Fenwick trees. There is currently no folder for data structures, can I make a folder "Cslib/Data/Lean/Fenwick"?

Presumably the work on Fenwick trees will be mainly about algorithms and data structures, judging from the Wikipedia entry on the subject?
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenwick_tree
If so, I would think the suggestion by @Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai would be more appropriate. I have the impression that the existing Cslib/Foundations/Data is for the more "theoretical" aspects of "data" which often has no computational contents (such as the existing OmegaSequence and Set).

Hard to say without seeing a PR, but maybe? Either way I'd like to (as I did last year) ask why we are suggesting Lean in a module name? This is unused in the example given and I never felt a good explanation was provided for this. It should be discussed before repeating that naming elsewhere.
(to @Basil Rohner I'd say don't worry about the module name too much to begin with since it's easily swapped out in review)
Isn't the Lean in the module name used to indicate that this is an algorithm written in Lean, as opposed to (say) Boole or some other models of computation which may appear in the future?
There’s a already a lean folder in core. In any case these algorithms are written in the writer monad. They aren’t pure lean functions.
